title: Reuse a dominating force of the same promise
motivation: In `bench_shootout_binarytrees_naive` `tree`, the argument promise for `depth - 1` forced and type-checked `depth` again, although the version had already forced it. The second force brought a checkpoint into the promise body. That checkpoint stopped `StrictifyPromise` from inlining the promise, so each recursive call allocated it. `permute` and `queens` had the same pattern.
solution: `DefiniteForce` now forwards a `force` to the result of a dominating `force` of the same SEXP. It looks through `AssumeType` and `Cast` chains, and it crosses only local promises (`prom-`). The earlier result type must be a subtype of the later one. `ElideTrivialAssume` also removes a type assumption whose result is unused, because only that result carries the assumption. Then `StrictifyPromise` can inline the promise, and `tree` passes an unboxed `R` instead of a promise.

files.repo-map.md: Names the new rules in the lines of `DefiniteForce.java` and `ElideTrivialAssume.java`, and adds an entry for the example `unforced_promise_overflow.R`.
files.server/src/main/java/org/prlprg/fir/opt/: Adds `dominatingForce`, which finds a dominating force of the same SEXP through assumptions and casts, across local promises only.
Removes an `AssumeType` that has no assignee or an unused assignee.
files.server/src/test/java/org/prlprg/fir/opt/: Adds tests for forwarding through local promises and assumption chains, and for the non-local, non-dominated, and narrower-type cases.
Adds tests that an unused type assumption is removed and that used, function, and constant assumptions stay.
files.server/src/test/resources/org/prlprg/exa: New example: a promise `d + 1L` that would overflow goes to a recursive call that returns without forcing it, so nothing warns.
